fine_lines.title: ever vs never
fine_lines.explanation_ar: ever تعني «في أي وقت من حياتك» وتأتي غالبًا في السؤال: Have you ever seen a zebra? أما never فتعني «أبدًا، ولا مرة» وتأتي في الجملة المنفية بدون not: I have never been to a zoo. لا تقل: I haven't never.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Ever" means "at any time in your life" and is mostly used in questions: Have you ever seen a zebra? "Never" means "not at any time" and makes the sentence negative without "not": I have never been to a zoo. Don't say "I haven't never".

examples.sentence: Have you ever been to a museum?
I have never seen an elephant.
She has never flown in a plane.

fine_lines.title: been to vs gone to
fine_lines.explanation_ar: have been to = ذهبت وعُدت (زيارة في حياتي). has gone to = ذهب وما زال هناك.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Have been to" = you visited and came back. "Has gone to" = the person went and is still there.

examples.sentence: I have been to the zoo three times.
Pete isn't here. He has gone to the store.

fine_lines.title: for vs since (with present perfect)
fine_lines.explanation_ar: for + مدة زمنية (for a year, for a long time). since + بداية الزمن (since 2015, since Monday).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Use "for" with a period of time (for a year, for a long time). Use "since" with the starting point (since 2015, since Monday).

examples.sentence: I have lived here for over a year.
I have lived here since last May.

grammar.title: Present perfect with ever and never
grammar.explanation_ar:
المضارع التام = have/has + التصريف الثالث (past participle). نستخدمه للحديث عن تجارب في حياتنا دون ذكر وقت محدد.
• السؤال: Have you ever + p.p.? → Have you ever seen sculptures in a garden?
• الإجابة بالإثبات: Yes, I have. I've visited that museum many times.
• النفي بـ never: I have never seen a garden of sculptures. I've never been to any zoos!
أفعال الدرس: live → lived, see → seen, fly → flown, be → been, know → known, write → written.
grammar.explanation_en:
Present perfect = have/has + past participle. We use it to talk about experiences in our life, without a specific time.
• Question: Have you ever + past participle? → Have you ever seen sculptures in a garden?
• Yes: Yes, I have. I've visited that museum many times.
• Negative with never: I have never seen a garden of sculptures. I've never been to any zoos!
Verbs from the lesson: live → lived, see → seen, fly → flown, be → been, know → known, write → written.
examples: Have you ever seen a real elephant?
I have never been to D.C.'s zoo.
I've visited that museum many times.
Jean has always liked American Indian culture.

grammar.title: Present perfect for life until now: for, always
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم المضارع التام أيضًا لشيء بدأ في الماضي وما زال مستمرًا: I have lived in Washington for a long time. ومع always: I have always loved plants (منذ زمن وحتى الآن).
grammar.explanation_en: We also use the present perfect for something that started in the past and is still true: I have lived in Washington for a long time. With "always": I have always loved plants (from the past until now).
examples: I have lived here for over a year.
I've known farm animals my whole life.

questions.question: Complete: "Have you ___ seen sculptures in a garden?"
questions.explanation_ar: في سؤال التجربة نستخدم ever: Have you ever …?
questions.explanation_en: In questions about experience we use "ever": Have you ever …?

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
choices: I have never been to a zoo.
I haven't never been to a zoo.
I never have be to a zoo.
I have never went to a zoo.
questions.explanation_ar: never تكفي للنفي، والتصريف الثالث لـ be هو been.
questions.explanation_en: "Never" already makes it negative, and the past participle of "be" is "been".

questions.question: What is the past participle of "fly"?
Complete: "I have lived here ___ over a year."
